name: Macedonian Orthodox Church Schism
summary: The 55-year break after the Macedonian Orthodox Church declared itself independent of the Serbian Orthodox Church in 1967, ended by its recognition in 2022.

start.label: Macedonian church declares independence; Serbia calls it schismatic

end.date: May–June 2022 (communion restored and autocephaly granted by Serbia)
end.label: Communion restored; Serbia grants autocephaly

key_dates.label: Niš agreement on union with Serbia rejected in Skopje
Bishop Jovan Vraniškovski, head of the Serbian-backed Ohrid Archbishopric, imprisoned

background.text: The Serbian church had governed the dioceses of Macedonia; in 1958, with support from Yugoslavia's communist government, it allowed a Macedonian church with its own head under the Serbian patriarch.

happened.text: In July 1967 a church council at Ohrid declared the Macedonian Orthodox Church autocephalous (fully independent), claiming the heritage of the medieval Archbishopric of Ohrid; the Yugoslav authorities supported the move.
The Serbian church declared the Macedonian church schismatic and its bishops outside the church, and no other Orthodox church recognized it.

participants.name: Dositej
participants.role: First head of the Macedonian Orthodox Church

participants.name: Serbian Orthodox Church
participants.role: Mother church that declared the schism

participants.name: Jovan Vraniškovski
participants.role: Bishop who left the Macedonian church to lead a Serbian-backed archbishopric; imprisoned

participants.name: Bartholomew I
participants.role: Ecumenical Patriarch who received the church back into communion in 2022

outcomes.text: On 9 May 2022 the Ecumenical Patriarchate received the church back into communion under the name Archdiocese of Ohrid; the Serbian church recognized it later that month and granted it autocephaly in June 2022, though its name remains disputed.

condemnations.by: Holy Assembly of Bishops of the Serbian Orthodox Church
condemnations.reason: The Macedonian church's declaration of autocephaly condemned as schismatic and its bishops cut off from communion

persecution.title: Prosecution of Bishop Jovan Vraniškovski
persecution.summary: After Jovan Vraniškovski accepted the Niš agreement and led an archbishopric under the Serbian church, the Macedonian church expelled him and the government of North Macedonia (then the Republic of Macedonia) prosecuted him. In 2004 he was imprisoned for 'inciting ethnic and religious hatred'; Amnesty International called him a prisoner of conscience.

responsible.name: Courts and police of the Republic of Macedonia
Macedonian Orthodox Church
responsible.role: Expelled him and pressed for action

persecution.outcome: Served prison terms in 2004–2006 and later.
